subject: history
topicDisplay: HL Regional Option: History of Europe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The French Revolution began in:
questions.explain: The French Revolution began in 1789, overthrowing the absolute monarchy.

questions.q: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of France in:
questions.explain: Napoleon became Emperor in 1804 after rising to power during the Revolution.

questions.q: The Congress of Vienna (1815) aimed to:
options: Restore stability and a balance of power after Napoleon
questions.explain: The Congress redrew Europe's map to restore order and balance after Napoleon's defeat.

questions.q: Germany was unified in 1871 under the leadership of:
questions.explain: Bismarck engineered German unification under Prussian leadership in 1871.

questions.q: The Renaissance was:
options: A revival of art, learning and classical ideas
questions.explain: The Renaissance (14th-16th c.) saw a flourishing of art, scholarship and humanism.

questions.q: The Protestant Reformation is traditionally dated to Martin Luther's actions in:
questions.explain: Luther's 95 Theses (1517) sparked the Reformation, splitting Western Christianity.

questions.q: The Enlightenment emphasised:
questions.explain: Enlightenment thinkers stressed reason, liberty and progress, influencing revolutions.

questions.q: The wave of revolutions across Europe in 1848 was driven mainly by:
questions.explain: The 1848 revolutions demanded liberal reforms and national self-determination.

questions.q: Italian unification (the Risorgimento) involved leaders such as:
questions.explain: Garibaldi, Cavour and Mazzini were central figures in unifying Italy by 1871.

questions.q: The First World War began in:
questions.explain: WWI began in 1914 following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

questions.q: The Russian Revolution of October 1917 brought to power the:
questions.explain: The Bolsheviks seized power in 1917, founding a communist state.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) is significant because it:
options: Punished Germany and sowed future resentment
questions.explain: Its harsh terms are widely seen as contributing to instability and WWII.

questions.q: The Second World War in Europe ended in:
questions.explain: Germany surrendered in May 1945, ending WWII in Europe.

questions.q: After 1945, the 'Iron Curtain' described:
options: The division of Europe into Western and Soviet blocs
questions.explain: The Iron Curtain symbolised the Cold War division of Europe.

questions.q: The Holocaust was:
options: The Nazi genocide of Jews and other groups
questions.explain: The Holocaust was the systematic Nazi murder of six million Jews and other victims.

questions.q: Appeasement in the 1930s was intended to:
options: Avoid war by conceding to Germany
questions.explain: Britain and France conceded to Hitler hoping to prevent another major war.

questions.q: A 'fief' in medieval Europe was:
options: Land granted in return for service
questions.explain: Fiefs were landholdings granted within the feudal system in exchange for obligations.

questions.q: The fall of the Berlin Wall (1989) symbolised:
options: The end of the Cold War division of Europe
questions.explain: The Wall's fall marked the collapse of communist control in Eastern Europe.

questions.q: Assessing why Germany, rather than Austria, led German unification examines:
questions.explain: Weighing the factors behind Prussian-led unification is an analysis of causation.

questions.q: Comparing the causes of the French Revolution and the Russian Revolution is an example of:
questions.explain: Comparing revolutions across time and place is a key analytical skill.

specSource: IB Diploma History guide (first assessment 2020); HL regional depth options (Paper 3): History of Europe
